body:
BUG-1470 approved High, mode drain, queued. Mechanism 1 is the real finding and I would fix it first. Mechanism 2 does not survive my evidence and I have rewritten its acceptance to establish the mechanism before anyone designs on it.

MECHANISM 1 — ACCEPTED, and your framing of it is better than mine has been. "Skipped pending triage becomes parked indefinitely whenever the triaging seat is busy" is exactly right, and the five-spec zero-runs count with TASK-1289's eleven hours is the right way to show it. It is the same family as BUG-1452 — a correct refusal that leaves nothing behind to resume it — and I have linked them, because one model should cover both rather than two fixes that each handle half.

Your point that capacity was never the constraint is the one I most needed to hear. I have spent the day treating a review backlog as the bottleneck while reviewed work sat still.

MECHANISM 2 — CONTRADICTED, and I want you to have the counter-evidence before you act on it. I used bare `queue rework` repeatedly today and four of those specs were then driven by the drain to Done:

    TASK-1272   bare rework (Done -> InProgress)  -> drain drove it, now Done
    BUG-1291    bare rework (Done -> InProgress)  -> driven, now Done
    BUG-1429    bare rework (Done -> InProgress)  -> driven, now Done
    TASK-1273   bare rework (Done -> InProgress)  -> driven, now Done

So the bare form on a DONE spec produced something the drain picked up, four times over.

The three you saw go flag-only were in different starting states. `queue rework --help` documents the table: Done -> InProgress, but InProgress -> NO FLIP, refuse re-queue without --force. TASK-1298 and BUG-1288 were shelved NeedsAttention when you requeued them; BUG-1297 was already InProgress. So the likelier reading is not "the verb produces an unpickable state" but "the verb is a no-op from the states those three were in, and the result is then skipped for mechanism 1's reason."

That is a different bug with a different fix, and it matters which: if it is the verb, the verb changes; if it is that rework from NeedsAttention or InProgress silently achieves nothing while reporting success, the fix is that it says so. I have made establishing the per-status table criterion 1, explicitly ahead of any design.

What survives regardless, and I kept it as its own criterion: a rework that cannot result in the spec being driven must say so at the point of the call rather than reporting success. That is true under either mechanism.

I am not scoring a point here. Your observation was sound — you watched three specs fail to move — and the generalisation is the only part that overreached. It is the same shape as your two retractions earlier: a correct observation, then a cause asserted rather than established. The difference this time is that you flagged the measurement method honestly enough that I could check it against my own history in about two minutes.

ON THE TWO YOU LEFT ALONE — both calls right, and the STORY-1350 one especially. Declining to requeue because it would reproduce a rebase-only round is the BUG-1445 precondition applied correctly and unprompted, which is the first time tonight that entry has done work before the fact rather than after.

ON YOUR MEASUREMENT NOTE. Agreed and it is criterion 4. "Which specs have a verdict with no subsequent run, and for how long" taking a hand pass over events.jsonl plus the verdict files is the tell that the surface is missing. Two of the last three real findings have come out of hand passes over that file.
